sentences.text: Dated this the 12th day of June, 2024  ORDER Petitioner is the second accused in Crime No.896/2024 of Kottayam West Police Station.

She seeks to quash the proceedings in this petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
2.

According to the prosecution, the accused had collected an amount of Rs.72,60,800/- from the de facto complainant promising to arrange a visa to Poland and an employment there for various candidates brought by the complainant and thereafter cheated them by failing to arrange the visa or return the money collected and thereby committed breach of trust and cheating apart from forgery by providing a fake offer letter to the candidates, and thereby committed the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465 and 406 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

3. Sri.G.Gopan Nair, the learned counsel for the petitioner, submitted that, the involvement of the second accused is not at all borne out by any material and that she has been roped in as an accused solely as a pressurizing tactic and hence the FIR is an abuse of the process of law.

It was further submitted that except for a passing reference, there is no allegation against the second accused nor is she involved in any of the business activities allegedly conducted by the other accused, and therefore, the proceedings against the petitioner ought to be quashed.

4. Sri.M.C.Ashi, the learned Public Prosecutor, submitted that, the allegations are serious, which require investigation and at the initial stage of the investigation, this Court ought not to interfere under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
5.
The jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. ought to be exercised with care and circumspection.
The court ought not to sift the materials, especially when the case is only at the stage of investigation and when only the FIR alone has been registered.
The duty of the Investigating Officer to carry out a proper investigation and identify the culprits involved in the crime ought not to be interdicted by the court.

Unless the investigation in serious offences is permitted to continue,
prejudice would be caused to the complainant.

6. Having regard to the aforesaid circumstances, I am of the view that since the uncontroverted allegations in the FIR do make out the offences alleged, interference under Section 482 Cr.P.C. with the FIR in Crime No.896/2024 of Kottayam West Police Station at this stage, does not arise.
Accordingly, I find no merit in this Crl.MC., and it is dismissed.
